[← Back to the lesson: Scaled dot-product attention](../scaled-dot-product-attention.qmd)

## Check your understanding

[Extended exercises on this topic](../exercises.qmd#attention).

1. A row of scores is $(2,0)$ and the key dimension is $d_k=4$. Calculate the softmax weights after scaling.

<details>
<summary>Show the reasoning</summary>

First divide the scores by $\sqrt{4}=2$, giving $(1,0)$. Softmax is approximately $(0.731,0.269)$. Scaling precedes normalization; the weights remain relative to the scores in this row only. The variant where one position is forbidden by a causal mask is covered in the self-check on [causal masking](../causal-masking.qmd).

</details>

2. A position receives an attention weight of $0.95$. Can we conclude that it makes the largest contribution to the output or is the primary cause of the prediction?

<details>
<summary>Show the reasoning</summary>

No. Before the output projection, its direct contribution is $0.95v_j$: its norm also depends on $\\lVert v_j\\rVert$, not only on the weight. The output projection, residual connections, normalization, and MLP then transform the signal further. A high weight is a relative aggregation weight, not a measure of causal importance. Studying causal effect requires an appropriate intervention-based analysis.

</details>
